title: A Ledger for the Uniform
premise: In 1913 London, Yara Nakamura, a Japanese-English chauffeur for suffragist Edith Marlowe, secretly reads the movement's letters and believes history is something that happens to other people. When a shell-shocked soldier named Tobias arrives carrying letters in the handwriting of Edith's brother Alistair—declared dead at Gallipoli years early and wrongly reported—Yara and Tobias are drawn into uncovering how Alistair survived, why his return was buried, and what Edith's own family concealed. As war looms and Edith faces imprisonment under the Cat and Mouse Act, Yara must decide who among this found family gets the last safe passage out of England before the century of certainty turns. The novel ends with Yara choosing to give her own berth to Tobias, staying behind to keep Edith's archive—and her chosen family—alive through the coming storm.
about_author: Quentin Pemberton is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suffragette correspondence in regional British collections. They write historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Other People's Words
chapters.summary: Yara drives Edith Marlowe through London on the eve of a mass suffrage march, sealing letters she has already read. Her POV establishes her creed: history happens elsewhere, to other people. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Grease and Ink
chapters.summary: In the garage, Yara mends the Daimler while memorizing a letter naming safe houses. POV shifts briefly to Edith, who suspects her driver reads everything and says nothing. Beat: mutual, unspoken respect between two women guarding secrets.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Service Entrance
chapters.summary: Tobias Finch arrives soaked and trembling, carrying a bundle of letters in Alistair Marlowe's unmistakable hand—Alistair, dead these three years. Yara's POV; the shock cracks her belief that history happens elsewhere. Beat: vertigo.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Edith examines the letters and goes white: they are recent, dated months ago, from a hospital in Malta. Yara watches grief and hope fight openly on her employer's face. Beat: the family myth begins to fracture.

chapters.title: What Tobias Carried
chapters.summary: Tobias, a former army clerk, explains he was ordered to burn the correspondence but kept it instead. His POV reveals survivor's guilt from a field hospital where Alistair saved him. Beat: two damaged strangers recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Yara proposes they treat the mystery like accounts: dates, names, sums. She begins a private ledger of evidence. Beat: her first act of agency—history can be entered, itemized, perhaps even changed.

chapters.title: A Brother, Properly Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Edith's POV: Alistair's farewell dinner in 1910, his shame at opposing her suffrage work, their unreconciled quarrel. Beat: regret that predates the war.

chapters.title: Malta, By Way of a Censor's Stamp
chapters.summary: The letters' postal marks suggest military censorship hid Alistair's survival to protect someone senior. Yara and Tobias trace the stamps. Beat: the machinery of empire revealed as banal paperwork.

chapters.title: The March That Turns Violent
chapters.summary: Yara drives Edith to a Hyde Park rally that ends in police batons and arrests. She abandons the car to pull Edith free. Beat: Yara stops observing history and touches it.

chapters.title: Cell Doors and Car Doors
chapters.summary: Edith, released after a night in Holloway, refuses to slow down. Yara argues for caution; Edith calls her a spectator. Their first real rupture. Beat: belonging offered and refused.

chapters.title: The Clerk Who Kept Copies
chapters.summary: Tobias locates his old superior, Major Renwick, now in the War Office, who burned the original file. Tobias's POV; he realizes he was meant to be the eraser. Beat: complicity and dread.

chapters.title: A Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Yara finds a marginal note in one letter—a woman's name, 'V.'—suggesting Alistair had help deserting his post. Beat: the dead man becomes complicated, human, possibly dishonorable.

chapters.title: Vera
chapters.summary: POV of Vera Calloway, a Maltese hospital nurse now working in London, who forged the death notice to free Alistair from blackmail by his commanding officer. Beat: another hidden historian, keeping her own ledger.

chapters.title: Tea with a Forger
chapters.summary: Yara meets Vera alone; the two women compare the ethics of altering records. Vera warns that Renwick will not let it stand. Beat: sisterhood across class and compromise.

chapters.title: The Cat and the Mouse
chapters.summary: Edith, weakened by hunger strikes, is released and rearrested under the new Act. Yara becomes her lifeline, driving between prison gates. Beat: devotion tested by exhaustion.

chapters.title: What the Letters Actually Say
chapters.summary: Reading the full correspondence aloud, the household learns Alistair stayed hidden to protect Vera and dozens of soldiers he exposed to scandal. Beat: grief transmuted into fierce pride.

chapters.title: Renwick's Card
chapters.summary: Major Renwick visits the Marlowe house with polite threats: drop the inquiry or Edith's record becomes 'complicated.' Yara's POV; fear arrives wearing a good coat. Beat: menace without violence.

chapters.title: The Berth
chapters.summary: Edith reveals an old arrangement: a paid passage to Canada, one berth, held for family fleeing scandal or worse. It becomes the novel's ticking clock as pressure mounts. Beat: safety quantified—one seat.

chapters.title: Everyone Counts Themselves Out
chapters.summary: Each character privately decides someone else deserves the berth: Edith names Yara, Yara names Edith, Tobias names both, Vera refuses to leave at all. Beat: love expressed as self-erasure.

chapters.title: Ledger Entries, Unsent
chapters.summary: Yara writes letters she'll never send—to her estranged father in Yokohama, to Alistair's ghost—weighing what family means when blood is absent. Beat: the theme of found family made explicit.

chapters.title: The Archive in the Coal Cellar
chapters.summary: Yara and Tobias hide the suffragette papers and Alistair's letters beneath the coal cellar, building a false wall. Beat: two people becoming custodians of memory together.

chapters.title: Renwick Closes In
chapters.summary: Renwick obtains a warrant pretext and has the house watched; Vera sends warning. Tension spikes as escape routes narrow. Beat: the noose of bureaucracy tightening.

chapters.title: Alistair Alive
chapters.summary: A telegram: Alistair himself is crossing from Marseille. The household prepares for a reunion three years premature. Beat: joy shadowed by terror of what his return will cost.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Dead Enough
chapters.summary: Alistair arrives gaunt and unrepentant; he and Edith collide over pride, politics, and the years lost. Yara observes the family she never had, warts blazing. Beat: reunion as reckoning.

chapters.title: Renwick's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Renwick offers terms: Alistair surrenders quietly, the record stays closed, and everyone walks away—or he destroys Edith with fabricated charges. Beat: the antagonist makes history personal.

chapters.title: Vera's Gamble
chapters.summary: Vera offers Renwick her own counter-evidence—the CO's blackmail ledger—in exchange for silence. Her POV shows the cost of forging a life. Beat: courage from the least protected.

chapters.title: Night Drive
chapters.summary: Yara drives Alistair and Vera toward the coast through police checkpoints, using her chauffeur's invisibility as camouflage. Beat: the observer becomes the engine of events.

chapters.title: Caught at the Toll
chapters.summary: They are stopped; Tobias takes the blame for the documents, claiming he acted alone, and is detained. Yara's guilt ignites into resolve. Beat: sacrifice by the newest member of the family.

chapters.title: Holloway Again
chapters.summary: Yara visits Tobias in custody and Edith in her cell on the same day, carrying messages between them like a living ledger. Beat: endurance as resistance.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Edith trades her silence on Renwick's CO scandal for Tobias's release—but the berth question returns with force: someone must still disappear before winter. Beat: bargains that feel like losses.

chapters.title: What Yara Decided at Sixteen
chapters.summary: Backstory chapter: Yara's arrival in England, disowned by her father, taken in by Edith's household. Explains why the berth matters so much. Beat: the wound beneath the competence.

chapters.title: The Last Sailing Before the Storm
chapters.summary: War rumors harden; the shipping line confirms the berth expires in ten days. All parties maneuver. Beat: time itself becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: Alistair Refuses
chapters.summary: Alistair announces he will surrender publicly and clear Vera's name, forfeiting any claim to the berth. Edith rages, then relents. Beat: honor as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Night of the Long Lists
chapters.summary: The household drafts and redrafts who should go: arguments, tears, laughter over cold supper. Yara listens and quietly reaches her decision. Beat: found family arguing its way into shape.

chapters.title: Berth for One
chapters.summary: Climax part one: Yara forges Edith's signature on the passage documents, assigning the berth to herself—then, at the dock, hands the ticket to Tobias, whose name Renwick still hunts. Beat: the choice the blurb promised.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Quay
chapters.summary: Renwick arrives to stop them; Edith publicly threatens to publish the blackmail ledger unless he stands down. He yields, defeated by exposure rather than force. Beat: victory by the very weapon of record-keeping.

chapters.title: The Ship That Takes Him
chapters.summary: Tobias sails; Yara watches until the funnel smoke dissolves. Grief and rightness share the same breath. Beat: letting go as an act of love.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Itemized
chapters.summary: Alistair testifies, Vera is vindicated, Edith resumes the fight. Yara closes her ledger with a final entry: 'History happened here. I was in it.' Beat: transformation completed.

chapters.title: The Empty Garage Bay
chapters.summary: Quiet epilogue-chapter: the household reorganizes around absence; Yara teaches a new girl to read the mail before sealing it, passing on the habit. Beat: continuity of care.

chapters.title: A Ledger for the Uniform
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Yara's POV, 1914's first week: war declared, the world tipping. She opens a fresh ledger titled with the book's name and writes the first line of the next story. Beat: memory kept, belonging chosen, the century turning.
